one_line: Late 8th–early 9th century Ganga king of Gangavadi, remembered for resisting Rashtrakuta expansion and for the war-elephant lore of Gajashtaka.

appearance.age_look: Mid-30s to early 40s, medium-tall, athletic but slightly lean from hardship, with a kingly bearing.
appearance.face: Oval face with a firm jaw, wheatish-brown complexion, straight nose, sharp dark eyes under slightly thick brows, a neatly trimmed short moustache and light stubble; default expression is calm and introspective, with a determined, steady gaze hinting at resilience in captivity.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair drawn back into a high knot at the back of the head (early medieval South Indian warrior style), with a narrow gold headband resting above the forehead; a thin cloth tie in deep maroon secures the knot, with a few short strands falling near the temples.
appearance.costume: Era-accurate early medieval South Indian royal attire: a long-sleeved, knee-length cotton tunic in muted off-white with a subtle woven border, worn over fitted brownish-red trousers; around his torso is a deep emerald-green angavastra-style shawl draped from the left shoulder across the chest and wrapped around the waist, its borders patterned with narrow gold and maroon stripes; over this he wears simple but dignified warrior-royal gear—broad, plain bronze armlets on the upper arms, matched bronze bangles, and a modest, flat, circular gold pendant on a dark cord; his waist is cinched with a wide, dark leather belt with a simple bronze buckle, from which hangs a small cloth pouch; on his feet are sturdy brown leather sandals with wrap-around straps over the ankles; the overall textile look is cotton with faint, traditional line patterns at the hems, avoiding heavy ornamentation to suggest a ruler hardened by conflict and imprisonment rather than ostentatious court luxury.
appearance.signature: A long, slightly curved South Indian iron sword in a plain dark scabbard, worn at his left hip, with a simple cross-guard and a wrapped leather hilt, accompanied by a small carved wooden elephant charm tied at the belt near the sword to allude to his Gajashtaka association.

ref_desc: Shivamara II is a wheatish-brown, oval-faced king with sharp dark eyes, short moustache, black hair in a high knot with a gold headband, wearing an off-white tunic, emerald-green shawl, brown-red trousers, bronze ornaments, sandals, and a plain curved sword with a small elephant charm at his belt.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character of Shivamara II of Gangavadi: a mid-30s South Indian king with a wheatish-brown oval face, sharp dark eyes, straight nose, short moustache and light stubble, black hair pulled into a high knot tied with a maroon cloth and a narrow gold headband above his forehead. He wears an early medieval Deccan royal-warrior outfit: a long-sleeved, knee-length off-white cotton tunic with subtle woven borders, fitted brownish-red trousers, and an emerald-green angavastra-like shawl draped from his left shoulder across his chest and wrapped around his waist, its borders edged with slim gold and maroon stripes. Add simple bronze armlets on his upper arms, bronze bangles, and a small flat gold pendant on a dark cord; his waist is held by a broad dark leather belt with a bronze buckle and a small cloth pouch. Put sturdy brown leather sandals with wrap-around ankle straps on his feet. At his left hip hangs a long, slightly curved South Indian iron sword in a plain dark scabbard with a wrapped leather hilt, and at the belt near the sword is a small carved wooden elephant charm referencing Gajashtaka. Use a palette of off-white, emerald green, maroon, brown leather, and bronze-gold, and keep his expression calm, introspective, and resolute, as if a proud ruler enduring captivity, presented clearly from head to toe for consistent redraws.
